Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

Position — walk-away:
No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.
Detection guidance:
"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The Agreement contains no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-inducement covenant binding Meridian Fieldworks. Searches for "solicit", "induce", "recruit", "hire", and "employ" return no restrictive covenant; the only hits are § 12.3, which expressly preserves our freedom to hire any person responding to general recruitment and confirms we have given no no-hire commitment, and unrelated references to Vendor personnel (§§ 3.1, 14.2, 30.1) that impose no hiring restriction on us. Rule:

Title: Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: MFN in our favour is welcome; an MFN that obliges us to give the Vendor best terms is not.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No MFN obligation on Customer (MFN pricing in Customer's favour is welcome).
Position — fallback:
MFN limited to a defined product, for 12 months, with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.

Open-ended obligation to extend to Vendor any better terms given to any third party.

Identify who benefits from the MFN. Flag only when Customer must offer Vendor terms no less favourable than those given to others, or must match third-party offers. If the Vendor grants Customer best pricing, mark compliant and do not redline.

Redline guidance:
Delete the obligation on Customer; keep any Vendor-granted MFN.

content.text:
**Finding: Deviation (high severity) — § 12.4**

§ 12.4 imposes on us a worldwide non-compete covering any product or service that competes with Copperleaf, running through the term plus 24 months. That breaches the walk-away threshold on two counts: an undefined scope ("any product or service that competes") and a post-term tail exceeding 12 months. It also flatly contradicts our protective § 12.3, in which Copperleaf acknowledges we have made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment.

**Redline (validated, preferred level):** delete § 12.4 in full, leaving § 12.3 to govern.

**Comment delivered:** "[Playbook] We cannot accept restrictions on the businesses we operate or the products we develop, buy or sell, so we have deleted the 24-month worldwide non-compete in § 12.4, which also directly contradicts § 12.3. If Copperleaf needs protection, we could consider a narrow alternative limited to a single named competing product during the term only (max 12 months), with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions."

No other restrictive covenants binding us appeared in the document; restrictions running against Copperleaf are unaffected.

Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence

Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with a carve-out for internal development and acquisitions.

Post-term non-compete longer than 12 months, or undefined scope ("any competing business").

Look for "shall not … develop/market/sell/engage in", "competing products", "compete with Vendor", field-of-use or territory restrictions binding Customer. Restrictions binding the Vendor are fine.

§ 12.4 binds us (Customer) with an undefined-scope, worldwide non-compete extending 24 months post-term — beyond the walk-away threshold (post-term restriction over 12 months and "any product or service that competes"). input.quote: 21.1 Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.
input.rationale: The cap is mutual but set at only one month of Fees "actually paid", far below the walk-away floor of six months' fees and below the preferred greater of 12 months' Fees and USD 1,000,000. Worse, "without exception" overrides the otherwise well-drafted Excluded Claims regime in 21.2–21.3, pulling indemnities, confidentiality, data-protection/security breaches, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement inside a one-month cap. The redline raises the basis to the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000 and restores the Excluded Claims carve-out; 21.3 already contains the required carve-outs and confirms Customer's payment obligations are not damages, so no further edit is needed.

proposal.summary: Raise mutual cap to greater of 12 months' Fees and USD 1,000,000 and subject it to the Excluded Claims carve-outs
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We raised the mutual cap to the greater of twelve months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, as a one-month cap is not a meaningful remedy. We also removed "without exception" so that the Excluded Claims in Section 21.3 — including indemnification, confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches — sit outside the cap; if needed, we can accept a straight twelve months' Fees cap with those carve-outs preserved.

Parties: we represent Meridian Fieldworks, Inc.; counterparty is Copperleaf Technology Ltd..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement imposes no most-favoured-nation obligation on Meridian Fieldworks:

- **§ 12.3** expressly records that "Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment" — a helpful affirmative disclaimer in our favour.
- **§ 7.1** binds Customer only to pay the Order Form Fees and constrains *Vendor* from adding unidentified charges.
- **§ 8.3** caps *Vendor's* renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3%.

Full-text searches for "most-favoured", "favourable/favorable", "no less favourable", "best price", "benchmark", and third-party matching language surfaced nothing beyond § 12.3. Nothing requires us to extend Copperleaf terms given to third parties or to match competing offers, so the preferred position is already met and no edit is warranted.

Note for the wider review (outside this rule): §§ 2.1 (take-or-pay minimum), 2.2 (sole and exclusive provider) and 12.4 (24-month non-compete on Customer) sit awkwardly against § 12.3's disclaimer and should be picked up under the exclusivity/non-compete and volume-commitment rules.

Rule:
ID: MFN
Title: Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: MFN in our favour is welcome; an MFN that obliges us to give the Vendor best terms is not.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No MFN obligation on Customer (MFN pricing in Customer's favour is welcome).
Position — fallback:
MFN limited to a defined product, for 12 months, with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
Position — walk-away:
Open-ended obligation to extend to Vendor any better terms given to any third party.
Detection guidance:
Identify who benefits from the MFN. Flag only when Customer must offer Vendor terms no less favourable than those given to others, or must match third-party offers. If the Vendor grants Customer best pricing, mark compliant and do not redline.

Redline guidance:
Delete the obligation on Customer; keep any Vendor-granted MFN.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The agreement contains no most-favoured-nation or best-terms undertaking running against Customer. Section 12.3 expressly confirms Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment, and the pricing provisions (§ 7.1 fixed Fees; § 7.2–7.5; § 8.3 capped renewal uplift) impose no obligation on Customer to extend Vendor terms given to third parties or to match third-party offers. A full-text search for "most-favoured", "favourable/favorable", "no less favourable", "best price", "benchmark", and third-party matching language returned no obligation burdening Customer. The only pricing-related constraints run against Vendor, which is in our favour. No redline required for this rule (other clauses such as §§ 2.1, 2.2 and 12.4 raise separate exclusivity/non-compete issues addressed under different rules).

Original paragraphs:
p0049: 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.

p0034: 8.3 On renewal, Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent. Vendor must give at least ninety days' written notice of an increase. No increase applies to prepaid periods.

A purchase order is an administrative convenience only and does not amend an Order Form or this Agreement.

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

content.text:
**Finding: Deviation (high severity) — EXCLUSIVITY**

Section 2.2 (p0013) makes Copperleaf our "sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term" — an unqualified, full-term exclusive dealing obligation binding us, with no category limit, no 12-month cap, and no performance-based exit. That sits at the playbook's walk-away position.

Aggravating context:
- **Section 12.3 (p0049)** has Vendor acknowledge that "Customer has made no exclusivity … or minimum-volume … commitment" — a direct internal contradiction, and the order-of-precedence clause (duplicate-numbered 2.2, p0014) does not resolve it.
- **Section 2.1 (p0012)** layers a USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay commitment on top, so exclusivity would leave us with no sourcing flexibility at all.

**Redline (validated, preferred level):** Section 2.2 becomes "Vendor will be a non-exclusive provider of hosted analytics services, and Customer may procure the same or similar services from any third party at any time." The comment offers the fallback (single defined category, 12 months, automatic termination on SLA or delivery failure) if Copperleaf pushes back.

Rule:
ID: EXCLUSIVITY
Title: Exclusivity obligations binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We keep the freedom to buy from other suppliers.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No exclusivity or "sole supplier" obligation on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Exclusivity limited to a defined product category and 12 months, ending automatically on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates.

Position — walk-away:
Exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit.
Detection guidance:
Phrases like "exclusive", "sole and exclusive provider", "shall purchase all of its requirements from", "shall not procure … from any third party". Exclusivity granted to Customer (e.g. Vendor won't serve our competitors) is acceptable and not a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback; keep any exclusivity that benefits Customer.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 2.2 imposes a full-term sole-supplier obligation on Customer for hosted analytics services, with no product-category limit, no time limit, and no performance-based exit. That is the walk-away position under the rule and directly contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity commitment. Combined with the take-or-pay volume commitment in Section 2.1, it eliminates our ability to source elsewhere. The exclusivity runs against us (not in our favour), so it is a deviation. Redline converts Vendor to a non-exclusive provider and expressly preserves our right to buy from third parties, per the preferred position; fallback (single category, 12 months, automatic termination on SLA/delivery failure) offered in the comment.

p0013: 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
p0049: 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.

input.quote: 21.1 Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.
input.rationale: The cap is mutual but set at only one month of Fees "actually paid", far below the walk-away floor of six months' fees and below the preferred greater of 12 months' Fees and USD 1,000,000. Worse, "without exception" overrides the otherwise well-drafted Excluded Claims regime in 21.2–21.3, pulling indemnities, confidentiality, data-protection/security breaches, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement inside a one-month cap. The redline raises the basis to the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000 and restores the Excluded Claims carve-out; 21.3 already contains the required carve-outs and confirms Customer's payment obligations are not damages, so no further edit is needed.

proposal.summary: Raise mutual cap to greater of 12 months' Fees and USD 1,000,000 and subject it to the Excluded Claims carve-outs
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We raised the mutual cap to the greater of twelve months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, as a one-month cap is not a meaningful remedy. We also removed "without exception" so that the Excluded Claims in Section 21.3 — including indemnification, confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches — sit outside the cap; if needed, we can accept a straight twelve months' Fees cap with those carve-outs preserved.

Parties: we represent Meridian Fieldworks, Inc.; counterparty is Copperleaf Technology Ltd..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

ops.oldText: 20.1 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services.
ops.newText: 20.1 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from and against any third-party claim to the extent arising out of (a) content or materials Customer provides to Vendor for use in the Services, or (b) Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

ops.text: 20.2 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services, Deliverables, or Vendor Technology infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to, or disclosure of, Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. 20.3 The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of the claim, tender control of the defence and settlement, and provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense; no settlement imposing a non-monetary obligation on, or an admission by, the indemnified Party may be made without its written consent, and the indemnified Party may participate with its own counsel at its own expense. 20.4 Vendor's obligation under Section 20.2(a) does not apply to the extent a claim arises from Customer's modification of the Services or Deliverables contrary to Vendor's documentation, combination with materials not supplied or recommended by Vendor, or Vendor's compliance with Customer's written specifications. 20.5 If a claim described in Section 20.2(a) arises or is reasonably likely, Vendor shall, at its expense, procure the right for Customer to continue using the affected item or modify or replace it with a functionally equivalent, non-infringing item. If Vendor cannot do so within thirty days, Customer may terminate the affected Services or Deliverables and receive a refund of Fees paid for them, including prepaid Fees for the terminated period.

payload.summary: Add Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity, indemnity procedure and IP remedies (Section 20.5); narrow Customer's indemnity
payload.comment: [Playbook] Section 20 currently contains only a broad Customer indemnity in Vendor's favour, so we added Vendor's defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, together with standard claim procedure and the infringement remedies Section 9.3 already assumes exist in Section 20.5. We also narrowed Customer's indemnity to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law; if needed, we can discuss a 3x annual Fees super-cap on Vendor's indemnity as a fallback.

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

input.summary: Add Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity, indemnity procedure and IP remedies (Section 20.5); narrow Customer's indemnity
input.comment: [Playbook] Section 20 currently contains only a broad Customer indemnity in Vendor's favour, so we added Vendor's defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, together with standard claim procedure and the infringement remedies Section 9.3 already assumes exist in Section 20.5. We also narrowed Customer's indemnity to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law; if needed, we can discuss a 3x annual Fees super-cap on Vendor's indemnity as a fallback.

ops.oldText: 20.1 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services.
ops.newText: 20.1 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from and against any third-party claim to the extent arising out of (a) content or materials Customer provides to Vendor for use in the Services, or (b) Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

ops.text: 20.2 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services, Deliverables, or Vendor Technology infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to, or disclosure of, Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. 20.3 The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of the claim, tender control of the defence and settlement, and provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense; no settlement imposing a non-monetary obligation on, or an admission by, the indemnified Party may be made without its written consent, and the indemnified Party may participate with its own counsel at its own expense. 20.4 Vendor's obligation under Section 20.2(a) does not apply to the extent a claim arises from Customer's modification of the Services or Deliverables contrary to Vendor's documentation, combination with materials not supplied or recommended by Vendor, or Vendor's compliance with Customer's written specifications. 20.5 If a claim described in Section 20.2(a) arises or is reasonably likely, Vendor shall, at its expense, procure the right for Customer to continue using the affected item or modify or replace it with a functionally equivalent, non-infringing item. If Vendor cannot do so within thirty days, Customer may terminate the affected Services or Deliverables and receive a refund of Fees paid for them, including prepaid Fees for the terminated period.

input.rationale: No non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-inducement covenant binds Meridian Fieldworks anywhere in the Agreement. Searches for "solicit", "induce", "recruit", "hire", "no-hire", and "employ" surface no restrictive covenant; the only relevant paragraph is § 12.3 (p0049), and the remaining "personnel" references (§§ 3.1, 14.2, 30.1) address Vendor responsibility for its own staff, not any hiring restriction on us. The quote is now expanded to include the operative freedom-to-hire language: § 12.3 expressly preserves our right to hire any person responding to general recruitment (functioning as the general-solicitation carve-out) and records that we have given no no-hire commitment. This satisfies the preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer), so the fallback's duration and carve-out parameters are inapplicable and no redline is warranted.

Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

Position — walk-away:
No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.
Detection guidance:
"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Meridian Fieldworks, Inc.; counterparty is Copperleaf Technology Ltd..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (critical) — § 21.1**

- **Issue:** The cap is mutual, but the basis is only one month of Fees *actually paid* — well below the 6-month walk-away floor. The trailing "without exception" also neutralises the Excluded Claims regime in §§ 21.2–21.3, dragging indemnities, confidentiality/data-protection/security breaches, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement inside a one-month cap.
- **Helpful existing language:** § 21.2 has a mutual exclusion of indirect damages with restoration/incident-response costs treated as direct; § 21.3 already lists the full carve-out set and confirms Customer's payment obligations are not damages. No edits needed there.
- **Redline (validated, preferred level):** § 21.1 now reads "Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed the greater of (a) Fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000." Fallback of a straight 12 months' Fees cap is offered in the comment.

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
The cap is mutual but set at only one month of Fees "actually paid", far below the walk-away floor of six months' fees and below the preferred greater of 12 months' Fees and USD 1,000,000. Worse, "without exception" overrides the otherwise well-drafted Excluded Claims regime in 21.2–21.3, pulling indemnities, confidentiality, data-protection/security breaches, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement inside a one-month cap. The redline raises the basis to the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000 and restores the Excluded Claims carve-out; 21.3 already contains the required carve-outs and confirms Customer's payment obligations are not damages, so no further edit is needed.

Original paragraphs:
p0082: 21.1 Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.

Resolved definitions:
Fees: 1.5 “Fees” means the recurring subscription fees, professional services fees, usage fees, and other amounts payable by Customer under an Order Form for the Services during the applicable period. Fees do not include taxes, reimbursable expenses, service credits, interest, damages, or a one-time implementation charge unless an Order Form expressly states otherwise.

Rendered redline:
p0082: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed the greater of (a) Fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000.

Comment:
[Playbook] We raised the mutual cap to the greater of twelve months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, as a one-month cap is not a meaningful remedy. We also removed "without exception" so that the Excluded Claims in Section 21.3 — including indemnification, confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches — sit outside the cap; if needed, we can accept a straight twelve months' Fees cap with those carve-outs preserved.

Deterministic checks:

Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

Position — walk-away:
No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.
Detection guidance:
"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
No non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-inducement covenant binds Meridian Fieldworks anywhere in the Agreement. Searches for "solicit", "induce", "recruit", "hire", "no-hire", and "employ" surface no restrictive covenant; the only relevant paragraph is § 12.3 (p0049), and the remaining "personnel" references (§§ 3.1, 14.2, 30.1) address Vendor responsibility for its own staff, not any hiring restriction on us. The quote is now expanded to include the operative freedom-to-hire language: § 12.3 expressly preserves our right to hire any person responding to general recruitment (functioning as the general-solicitation carve-out) and records that we have given no no-hire commitment. This satisfies the preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer), so the fallback's duration and carve-out parameters are inapplicable and no redline is warranted.

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.

Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.

"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Parties: we represent Meridian Fieldworks, Inc.; counterparty is Copperleaf Technology Ltd..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
§ 8.2 matches our preferred position exactly: automatic renewals are limited to successive twelve-month periods, Customer may opt out on only thirty days' written notice, and Vendor must send a renewal reminder sixty days beforehand — with the opt-out deadline extended if the reminder is missed, which is better than our ask. § 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of US CPI and three percent, with ninety days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods, meeting the preferred price-predictability requirement. No auto-renewal escalator or longer notice window appears elsewhere (searches for "renew" and "increase" return only §§ 8.1–8.3), and § 8.1's three-year term is the initial term, not a multi-year auto-renewal. No redline needed.

p0033: 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.
p0034: 8.3 On renewal, Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent. input.quote: 20. INDEMNIFICATION 20.1 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services.
input.rationale: Section 20 is entirely one-sided: the only indemnity runs from Customer to Vendor and covers "every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services". There is no Vendor indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and no claim-handling procedure. Section 9.3 confirms the gap by cross-referencing infringement remedies "required by Section 20.5", which does not exist. Section 21.3 already treats indemnification obligations and IP infringement as Excluded Claims, so the missing Vendor indemnity is the operative gap. We inserted the preferred Vendor indemnity with standard procedure, customary IP exclusions and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies as Section 20.5, and narrowed Customer's indemnity to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

proposal.summary: Add Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity, indemnity procedure and IP remedies (Section 20.5); narrow Customer's indemnity
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 20 currently contains only a broad Customer indemnity in Vendor's favour, so we added Vendor's defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, together with standard claim procedure and the infringement remedies Section 9.3 already assumes exist in Section 20.5. We also narrowed Customer's indemnity to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law; if needed, we can discuss a 3x annual Fees super-cap on Vendor's indemnity as a fallback.

input.quote: 20. INDEMNIFICATION 20.1 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services.
input.rationale: Section 20 is entirely one-sided: the only indemnity runs from Customer to Vendor and covers "every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services". There is no Vendor indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and no claim-handling procedure. Section 9.3 confirms the gap by cross-referencing infringement remedies "required by Section 20.5", which does not exist. Section 21.3 already treats indemnification obligations and IP infringement as Excluded Claims, so the missing Vendor indemnity is the operative gap. We inserted the preferred Vendor indemnity with standard procedure, customary IP exclusions and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies as Section 20.5, and narrowed Customer's indemnity to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Rule:
ID: GOVLAW
Title: Governing law and venue
Kind: parametric
Summary: Accepted laws are New York, Delaware, California, or England and Wales; courts, not foreign arbitration.
Severity: medium
Category: governing-law
Position — preferred:
Laws of the State of New York; exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County.
Position — fallback:
Delaware or California law and courts; or the laws of England and Wales with the courts of London.
Position — walk-away:
Vendor's home jurisdiction outside the accepted list with exclusive foreign venue, or mandatory arbitration seated abroad.
Detection guidance:
Find the governing-law clause; extract jurisdiction and dispute forum; note any arbitration seat.
Redline guidance:
Replace only the jurisdiction words and forum; keep the rest of the sentence intact.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Section 28.1 selects New York law and Section 28.2 gives exclusive jurisdiction to the state and federal courts in New York County, which is precisely our preferred position. No arbitration provision appears anywhere in the document (search for "arbitration" returned no results), so there is no foreign seat concern. The pre-filing escalation in 28.3 is mutual and expressly does not delay urgent relief or limitations-preserving filings, and 28.2 preserves each Party's ability to seek temporary injunctive relief elsewhere to protect confidential information or IP. No redline needed.

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Parties: we represent Meridian Fieldworks, Inc.; counterparty is Copperleaf Technology Ltd..

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

Parties: we represent Meridian Fieldworks, Inc.; counterparty is Copperleaf Technology Ltd..

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Parties: we represent Meridian Fieldworks, Inc.; counterparty is Copperleaf Technology Ltd..

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

input.summary: Add Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity, indemnity procedure and IP remedies (Section 20.5); narrow Customer's indemnity
input.comment: [Playbook] Section 20 currently contains only a broad Customer indemnity in Vendor's favour, so we added Vendor's defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, together with standard claim procedure and the infringement remedies Section 9.3 already assumes exist in Section 20.5. We also narrowed Customer's indemnity to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law; if needed, we can discuss a 3x annual Fees super-cap on Vendor's indemnity as a fallback.

ops.oldText: 20.1 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services.
ops.newText: 20.1 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from and against any third-party claim to the extent arising out of (a) content or materials Customer provides to Vendor for use in the Services, or (b) Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

ops.text: 20.2 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services, Deliverables, or Vendor Technology infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to, or disclosure of, Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. 20.3 The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of the claim, tender control of the defence and settlement, and provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense; no settlement imposing a non-monetary obligation on, or an admission by, the indemnified Party may be made without its written consent, and the indemnified Party may participate with its own counsel at its own expense. 20.4 Vendor's obligation under Section 20.2(a) does not apply to the extent a claim arises from Customer's modification of the Services or Deliverables contrary to Vendor's documentation, combination with materials not supplied or recommended by Vendor, or Vendor's compliance with Customer's written specifications. 20.5 If a claim described in Section 20.2(a) arises or is reasonably likely, Vendor shall, at its expense, procure the right for Customer to continue using the affected item or modify or replace it with a functionally equivalent, non-infringing item. If Vendor cannot do so within thirty days, Customer may terminate the affected Services or Deliverables and receive a refund of Fees paid for them, including prepaid Fees for the terminated period.

Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

input.summary: Add Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity, indemnity procedure and IP remedies (Section 20.5); narrow Customer's indemnity
input.comment: [Playbook] Section 20 currently contains only a broad Customer indemnity in Vendor's favour, so we added Vendor's defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, together with standard claim procedure and the infringement remedies Section 9.3 already assumes exist in Section 20.5. We also narrowed Customer's indemnity to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law; if needed, we can discuss a 3x annual Fees super-cap on Vendor's indemnity as a fallback.

ops.oldText: 20.1 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services.
ops.newText: 20.1 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from and against any third-party claim to the extent arising out of (a) content or materials Customer provides to Vendor for use in the Services, or (b) Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

ops.text: 20.2 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services, Deliverables, or Vendor Technology infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to, or disclosure of, Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. 20.3 The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of the claim, tender control of the defence and settlement, and provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense; no settlement imposing a non-monetary obligation on, or an admission by, the indemnified Party may be made without its written consent, and the indemnified Party may participate with its own counsel at its own expense. 20.4 Vendor's obligation under Section 20.2(a) does not apply to the extent a claim arises from Customer's modification of the Services or Deliverables contrary to Vendor's documentation, combination with materials not supplied or recommended by Vendor, or Vendor's compliance with Customer's written specifications. 20.5 If a claim described in Section 20.2(a) arises or is reasonably likely, Vendor shall, at its expense, procure the right for Customer to continue using the affected item or modify or replace it with a functionally equivalent, non-infringing item. If Vendor cannot do so within thirty days, Customer may terminate the affected Services or Deliverables and receive a refund of Fees paid for them, including prepaid Fees for the terminated period.

input.quote: 20. INDEMNIFICATION 20.1 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services.
input.rationale: Section 20 is entirely one-sided: the only indemnity runs from Customer to Vendor and covers "every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services". There is no Vendor indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and no claim-handling procedure. Section 9.3 confirms the gap by cross-referencing infringement remedies "required by Section 20.5", which does not exist. Section 21.3 already treats indemnification obligations and IP infringement as Excluded Claims, so the missing Vendor indemnity is the operative gap. We inserted the preferred Vendor indemnity with standard procedure, customary IP exclusions and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies as Section 20.5, and narrowed Customer's indemnity to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

input.quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: Compliant with the preferred position: no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-inducement covenant binds Meridian Fieldworks anywhere in the Agreement. Searches for "solicit" (no hits), "induce" (no hits), "recruit", "hire", "no-hire", and "employ" surface only § 12.3 (p0049) plus unrelated references (§ 1.2 employment law, § 18.1 employer's liability insurance) and "personnel" provisions (§§ 1.4, 3.1, 14.2, 30.1) that allocate Vendor's responsibility for its own staff rather than restrict our hiring. § 12.3 goes further in our favour: it preserves our right to hire any person responding to general recruitment — the equivalent of, and broader than, the fallback's general-advertising carve-out — and records that we have made no no-hire commitment. The fallback parameters (12-month duration, general-solicitation and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, no no-hire) are conditions for narrowing a covenant that binds us; because none exists, those deterministic checks are non-probative here and cannot be "fixed" without manufacturing a restriction on ourselves. No redline is proposed, since any edit would be adverse to our client.

Kind: presence

No non-solicit on Customer.

Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.

"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 9.4 on its own meets the preferred position: Customer may terminate for convenience on thirty days' notice with a refund of prepaid Fees, and Vendor has no reciprocal convenience right during a committed term. However, Section 2.1 imposes a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment expressly "without reduction or termination rights," which conflicts with and could be read to override Section 9.4, leaving us locked into a multi-year spend with no effective convenience exit (the walk-away position). There is no order-of-precedence clause to resolve the conflict. The minimal fix is to make the Section 2.1 minimum expressly subject to our termination rights and reduce it pro rata on termination, leaving Section 9.4 intact.

Parties: we represent Meridian Fieldworks, Inc.; counterparty is Copperleaf Technology Ltd..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 9.4 on its own meets the preferred position: Customer may terminate for convenience on thirty days' notice with a refund of prepaid Fees, and Vendor has no reciprocal convenience right during a committed term. However, Section 2.1 imposes a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment expressly "without reduction or termination rights," which conflicts with and could be read to override Section 9.4, leaving us locked into a multi-year spend with no effective convenience exit (the walk-away position). There is no order-of-precedence clause to resolve the conflict. The minimal fix is to make the Section 2.1 minimum expressly subject to our termination rights and reduce it pro rata on termination, leaving Section 9.4 intact.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Meridian Fieldworks, Inc.; counterparty is Copperleaf Technology Ltd..

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.

Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.

Category: assignment

Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

**Finding (final): Compliant** — no redline, no counterparty comment.

The only change in this pass is a fuller evidentiary rationale; the substance and status are unchanged, because the verifier's own narrative confirms there is no directional or drafting defect to correct.

On the recurring "general-solicitation carve-out present: failed" check: I have not attempted to satisfy it, and I recommend it be treated as inapplicable rather than repaired. That check tests a fallback parameter — the shape of a non-solicit that binds the Customer. No such covenant exists here:

- "solicit" and "induce" return zero hits document-wide.
- "hire"/"recruit"/"no-hire" return only § 12.3, which runs in our favour.
- The remaining "personnel" provisions (§§ 1.4, 3.1, 14.2, 30.1) allocate Vendor's responsibility for its own staff; § 1.2 and § 18.1 are employment-law and insurance references.

The only way to make that heuristic pass would be to insert a non-solicit on ourselves and then carve out general advertising — i.e. to create a restriction on Meridian Fieldworks where the counterparty asked for none. That would be adverse to our client, so I've declined. § 12.3's "hiring any person who responds to general recruitment" already delivers the protection the carve-out is designed to secure, and does so more broadly.

Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

Position — walk-away:
No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.
Detection guidance:
"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Compliant with the preferred position: no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-inducement covenant binds Meridian Fieldworks anywhere in the Agreement. Searches for "solicit" (no hits), "induce" (no hits), "recruit", "hire", "no-hire", and "employ" surface only § 12.3 (p0049) plus unrelated references (§ 1.2 employment law, § 18.1 employer's liability insurance) and "personnel" provisions (§§ 1.4, 3.1, 14.2, 30.1) that allocate Vendor's responsibility for its own staff rather than restrict our hiring. § 12.3 goes further in our favour: it preserves our right to hire any person responding to general recruitment — the equivalent of, and broader than, the fallback's general-advertising carve-out — and records that we have made no no-hire commitment. The fallback parameters (12-month duration, general-solicitation and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, no no-hire) are conditions for narrowing a covenant that binds us; because none exists, those deterministic checks are non-probative here and cannot be "fixed" without manufacturing a restriction on ourselves. No redline is proposed, since any edit would be adverse to our client.

p0049: 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
